A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLaMA fine-tuning experiments, benchmark accuracies, training efficiency measurements, low-data comparisons and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluated Prompt Tuning, IA3 and VeRA baselines in Table 2.

M1.justification: Both versions retain separate prompt/token softmax operations, the tanh gate, frozen backbone and nonlinear prompts generated through a shared two-layer MLP. Equations (1)–(21) describe the same procedures.

E1.justification: Training remains on Alpaca, with evaluation on ARC Easy/Challenge, MMLU, HellaSwag and TruthfulQA. The low-data evaluation coverage and Appendix C examples are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Prompt Tuning, IA3 and VeRA as evaluated LLaMA-7B comparators, substantially broadening the PEFT comparison beyond full fine-tuning and LoRA. Existing comparator participation is retained.

E3.justification: The stated model sizes, prompt lengths and insertion layers, training hyperparameters, five-epoch budget, zero-shot/10-shot evaluations and training-data fractions remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same test counts and prompt templates.

E4.justification: The linear-versus-nonlinear comparison, training-data sensitivity analysis in Figures 2–3 and qualitative cases in Table 5 are retained. The added PEFT baseline scores do not introduce a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run summaries, confidence intervals or statistical tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds LLaMA-7B average accuracies of 47.48 for Prompt Tuning, 46.04 for IA3 and 45.19 for VeRA; the nonlinear model's 53.28 remains unchanged. Retained numerical entries, plotted data and qualitative answers match. v3 also removes the textual 8.28/9.03-point advantages comparing its 13B model against 7B full fine-tuning/LoRA.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a mathematical comparison using cited logarithmic convergence rates and exponential sample requirements for random-initialized attention versus the retained polynomial requirements for zero-initialized attention. The existing definitions, assumptions, theorem statements and Appendix A proofs are unchanged apart from numbering and citation formatting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the MoE connection, optimal prompt/gating estimation, extension to nonlinear prompts and empirical advantages of zero-initialized attention.

C2.justification: v3 makes the sample-efficiency rationale explicit and removes the cross-backbone superiority discussion. Its new Figure 3 caption overgeneralizes nonlinear prompts as consistently best, despite the retained plot and text showing linear prompts ahead at 1% training data. The substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3's abstract adds a public-implementation statement and GitHub hyperlink, providing access information absent from v2. Existing hardware, hyperparameters, training times and prompt templates are retained; repository contents cannot be assessed from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations concerning quadratic gating, VeRA, IA3, DuDE and multimodal models. Appendix B expands its discussion of Gaussian, sigmoid-gated and hierarchical MoE theory. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose is retained. v2's nonlinear-prompts section becomes Section 4.2, several explanatory passages and the baseline list are revised, references move before the supplement, and impact and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column ICML main-text layout, reflows the appendices and relocates/resizes figures and tables. Table 2 gains baseline rows and Figures 2–3 receive expanded captions. The underlying figure artwork and plotted data are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added PEFT comparisons, implementation link and explicit sample-complexity comparison modestly strengthen empirical context, access information and explanation. Removing the misleading 13B-versus-7B superiority passage also helps. These gains outweigh the limited new inconsistency in Figure 3's caption, which overlooks the retained 1% exception; the method, primary results and proofs remain unchanged.
